policy: Nothing here is applied silently: tools/build_webkit_jsc.py verifies the SHA-256 of each file before the patch (or accepts the recorded result), applies it, verifies the result, and records it in the configure fingerprint. Add an entry only with a reason and a removal condition (docs/porting/crtweb_porting.md).

patches.reason: WTF::RawHex gives int64_t/uint64_t their own constructors only for CPU(ADDRESS32) or OS(DARWIN); elsewhere it assumes int64_t is intptr_t (true for Linux/Bionic LP64). CRT presents macOS to WebKit as a Linux-shaped platform (no __APPLE__), but the compiler's integer types stay Darwin's (int64_t is long long, intptr_t is long): clang's own arm_acle.h/arm_neon.h and builtins require uint64_t == __UINT64_TYPE__, so the typedef cannot be changed (tried: clang crashed). RawHex(uint64_t) was therefore ambiguous in JavaScriptCore/tools/Integrity.cpp. The patch adds one more condition, selected by -DWTF_CRT_INT64_IS_LONG_LONG which the harness passes on macOS.
patches.remove_when: WebKit selects the int64_t overloads by type identity (std::is_same_v<int64_t, intptr_t>) instead of OS(DARWIN), or CRT presents macOS to WTF as OS(DARWIN) without pulling in Apple SDK code.

patches.reason: JavaScriptCore's inline assembler for the offlineasm LLInt and its thunks takes the assembler syntax from OS(DARWIN): the `_` symbol prefix (SYMBOL_STRING), `.private_extern _x` versus `.hidden x` (HIDE_SYMBOL), the local label prefix `L` versus `.L`, `.alt_entry`, and the absence of `.cfi_startproc` in the global asm blocks. Those are properties of the Mach-O object format, not of the OS, but CRT presents macOS to WebKit as a Linux-shaped platform (no __APPLE__; see 0001), so the ELF spellings were chosen and would not link or assemble. The patch ORs one more condition, selected by -DWTF_CRT_MACHO_ASM which the harness passes on macOS in baseline-jit mode, into those conditionals (the three in WTF/InlineASM.h, the alt-entry and two cfi conditionals in llint/LowLevelInterpreter.cpp, the `#if OS(DARWIN)` guard offlineasm itself writes into LLIntAssembly.h, and the two `#if OS(DARWIN)` guards arm64.rb writes for Mach-O versus ELF relocation specifiers (`@PAGE`/`@GOTPAGE` versus `:lo12:`/`:got:`)). offlineasm also emits ELF `.size`/`.type` debug directives whenever CMake passes --binary-format=ELF, which it does for CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME Linux, so asm.rb additionally skips them when the environment variable WTF_CRT_MACHO_ASM is set (the harness sets it).
patches.remove_when: WebKit keys the assembler syntax on the object format (__MACH__/__ELF__/_WIN32) instead of OS(DARWIN), or CRT presents macOS as OS(DARWIN) without Apple SDK code.

files.license_basis: directory-level license file Source/JavaScriptCore/COPYING.LIB (GNU Library GPL, LGPL-2); the file has no header of its own

patches.reason: CRT presents Windows to WebKit as a Linux-shaped platform (libcrtweb/cmake/crt_webkit_platform.cmake), so JavaScriptCore's offlineasm and inline assembly take their ELF branches, but the object format is COFF and the assembler rejects the ELF-only forms (found by the Windows baseline-jit build: `.hidden`, `.size` and `.type name, function` are `unknown directive`/`expected absolute expression`, `.previous` is an unknown directive, and a `name@plt` reference does not exist in COFF). Selected by -DWTF_CRT_COFF_ASM (compiler side) and the WTF_CRT_COFF_ASM environment variable (offlineasm side), both set by tools/build_webkit_jsc.py on Windows: HIDE_SYMBOL expands to nothing, GLOBAL_REFERENCE is the plain symbol, the ELF debug directives are not emitted, and the `.previous` after the probe trampolines and the unary-double thunks (an ELF section-stack directive; nothing follows them in the same asm block) is dropped. Mach-O has its own variant (0002).
patches.remove_when: WebKit selects these directives by object format (COFF/ELF/Mach-O) instead of OS(), or CRT presents Windows to WTF as OS(WINDOWS) without pulling in windows.h and the Microsoft C runtime.

patches.reason: CRT presents macOS to WebKit as OS(LINUX) to select the Bionic/Linux-shaped source surface, but generated code still follows the actual Darwin arm64 object and calling-convention ABI. ARM64Registers.h's Linux branch marks x18 allocatable, while Darwin reserves x18 as the platform register. Under FTL/B3 register pressure that mismatch let generated code use x18 across a runtime call and produced a null-address write near operationStringFromCharCode. The harness defines WTF_CRT_DARWIN_ARM64_ABI only for macOS arm64, selecting WebKit's existing non-Linux register table without enabling Apple SDK source branches; Linux/aarch64 is unchanged.
patches.remove_when: WebKit derives the x18 reservation from the target ABI/object format rather than OS(LINUX), or CRT can select WebKit's Darwin ABI traits independently of its Apple SDK source surface.

files.license_basis: no header of its own; the build files around it in Source/cmake carry the Apple BSD-2-Clause notice (47 of the directory's 96 files; none carry another license), and the file belongs to the same Apple-authored CMake build system

patches.reason: WebKitCommon.cmake accepts only the ports in ALL_PORTS and stops with 'Please choose which WebKit port to build' for any other -DPORT. The CRT port is a new port (Source/cmake/OptionsCRT.cmake and the per-module PlatformCRT.cmake files are new CRT-owned files, libcrtweb/port); its name has to be in that list. Everything else the port needs is selected by file name (Options${PORT}.cmake, Platform${PORT}.cmake) or by -DWTF_PLATFORM_CRT=1, as the PlayStation port does, so this is the only change to an existing file for milestone B1.
patches.remove_when: Never as long as CRT carries its own port: a port that is not upstream has to be registered. It is a one-line, rebase-friendly change.

license_policy.rule: A file this manifest modifies keeps its upstream license and header; the patch is a derivative under that license, so every entry records the class of the modified file (from tools/scan_webkit_headers.py) and it must be one CRT can carry: LGPL-2/2.1 (WebKit's own LGPL code), BSD-2/3-Clause (Apple's and most WebKit code) or another permissive class. A file CRT adds is a *new CRT-owned file*, listed under new_files with the project default license (LICENSE.md, BSD-2-Clause) and its header. Never mix: no CRT code is added to an LGPL file beyond the patch itself.
allowed_for_modified_files: no-license-header (only with a license_basis naming the directory-level license file)

new_files.purpose: the port's options (B1: JSCOnly's, plus the BUILDING_CRT__/WTF_PLATFORM_CRT identity)
